statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk stays in the watch band, below the block threshold, while the environment remains high-stress and semiconductor and breadth confirmation is absent.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays WATCH. The published danger window covers the quarter-end cash close from 19:00Z to 20:00Z, where power-hour flow and final-day-of-Q3 market-on-close imbalances overlap; Micron's fiscal Q4 report follows shortly after that close.
headline: Nasdaq-100 grinds to a marginal new session high while semiconductors lag and long-end yields sit at session highs into the quarter-end close
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30592.98, up 253.65 points or 0.84%, after printing a marginal new session high at 30630.45; it now sits about 38 points below that high, having opened at 30421.68 with a 30415.16 session low. The index is therefore holding the upper half of a 215-point two-way range rather than extending in a straight line, and the earlier retracement from the 30617.74 area was absorbed. Confirmation is conspicuously absent. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is at 12588.73, down 0.32% and close to its 12555.65 session low after reaching 12731.10 earlier, so the sector that normally leads a Nasdaq-100 advance is near the bottom of its own range while the index is near the top of its. Breadth is narrow: the Dow is down about 0.11% and the Russell 2000 up only fractionally, while the Nasdaq Composite is up roughly 1%. The rates picture is the main stress input. The 10-year yield is 5.29%, at the top of its 5.20-5.29 daily range, and the 30-year is 5.64% at its session high, close to its highest since 2002, a bear steepening against a 2-year near 4.92% on the latest H.15 daily figures. WTI is $91.50, up 2.37%, with crude holding near the upper end of its range. Volatility is not corroborating stress, however: the VIX has eased to 15.87, down 1.06% and in the lower part of a 15.62-16.32 range. Today's data were mixed but net supportive for equities and unsupportive for the long end: August core PCE rose 0.2% monthly against about 0.3% expected with headline PCE at 3.4% year over year against 3.7% expected, while ADP private payrolls added 90,000 against 70,000 expected, Chicago PMI jumped to 58.8 against 51.2 expected and final Q2 GDP growth was 2.2%. Traders trimmed October rate-hike odds to roughly 35-41% from around half before the release. Because the observed index path shows a contained range with absorbed pullbacks, and because semiconductors, the Dow and the VIX all decline to confirm the advance, the evidence does not establish the persistent mean-reversion failure that Tail measures; the diverging cross-asset picture, multi-decade-high long-end yields and firm energy raise Stress instead. Two scheduled discontinuities close the session: this is the final session of Q3, so quarter-end rebalancing concentrates two-way imbalance risk into the 20:00Z cash close, and Micron reports fiscal Q4 results shortly after it with the call scheduled for 20:30Z.

lookbackSummary: Published Claude assessments over the preceding 24 hours held Tail between 15 and 23. The mapping was green EA_ON from the late European session on September 29 through the Asian and European hours of September 30, with Stress easing from the mid-70s to about 65 overnight. The state returned to the watch band from 12:35Z as the US pre-open and the August PCE release approached, and Tail then firmed steadily through the cash session to 22 in the 14:00Z hour and 23 in the 15:00Z hour as long-end yields reversed higher.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to hold at 23 in the current hour, ease to 22 through the mid-afternoon lull, then widen to 24 across the 19:00Z-20:00Z power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, where final-day-of-Q3 market-on-close imbalances overlap Micron's post-close fiscal Q4 report. It eases through the late-US digestion hours, returns to the low band from 23:00Z and reaches its floor at 16 in the quietest late-Asian stretch, before firming again through the European session of October 1 and into the 12:30Z jobless claims release, the 13:30Z US cash open and the 14:00Z ISM Manufacturing print, which peaks the second half of the window at 23 before easing to 22. No forecast hour reaches the 25 block threshold. Non-farm payrolls on October 2 falls beyond this window.
